title: Live log tailing
intro: Work from the module directory. Fixtures: `app.log` (current), `app.log.1` and `app.log.2` (rotated), `archive_msg.txt.gz` (compressed), and `journalctl_sample.txt` (simulated systemd journal).

questions.prompt: Count the total number of lines across all `app.log*` files in the module directory (current log plus all rotated copies). How many lines are there in total?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
cat app.log app.log.1 app.log.2 | wc -l
# or
wc -l app.log* | tail -1
```

`app.log` has 3, `app.log.1` has 3, `app.log.2` has 1 — total **7**.

questions.prompt: Search all `app.log*` files for `ERROR` entries. Which rotation suffix (`.log`, `.log.1`, or `.log.2`) contains the only `ERROR` line?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -l 'ERROR' app.log*
```

Only `app.log.1` contains an `ERROR` entry — it's the rotated file from the previous run.

questions.prompt: The `journalctl_sample.txt` file simulates systemd journal output. How many lines in it mention the process `nginx`?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -c 'nginx' journalctl_sample.txt
```

Three entries: `nginx.service` started, an upstream ERROR, and a slow-cache WARN.

questions.prompt: Decompress `archive_msg.txt.gz` and print its content to stdout. What is the single line of text inside?
The `journalctl_sample.txt` records a successful SSH login. What is the source IP address of the accepted connection?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep 'Accepted' journalctl_sample.txt | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'
```

The line reads: `Accepted publickey for ops from 198.51.100.7 port 22 ssh2`.

questions.prompt: Count `ERROR` entries across all `app.log*` files. How many are there in total?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -r 'ERROR' app.log* | wc -l
# or: grep -c 'ERROR' app.log* | awk -F: '{sum+=$2} END{print sum}'
```

Only `app.log.1` has one ERROR entry.

questions.prompt: The journal sample records an SSH authentication failure. What username was the attacker attempting to access?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep 'authentication failure' journalctl_sample.txt
```

The line ends with `invalid user scanner`.

questions.prompt: What is the log message (the part after the severity level) in the very last line of `app.log.1`?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
tail -n 1 app.log.1 | awk '{print $3, $4}'
# or:
tail -n 1 app.log.1
```

The last line is `2026-05-13T13:00:16Z INFO retry scheduled` — the message is `retry scheduled`.

questions.prompt: The `journalctl_sample.txt` begins with a header showing the log time range. What is the end timestamp of that range? (Format: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, no timezone.)
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
head -n 1 journalctl_sample.txt
```

The header line reads: `-- Logs begin at … end at Wed 2026-05-13 14:05:00 UTC. --`

questions.prompt: One cron entry appears in the journal sample. What command does it execute? (Extract just the command path from inside the parentheses.)
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep 'cron' journalctl_sample.txt | grep -oP 'CMD \(\K[^)]+'
# or: awk with field split
```

The cron line reads: `(root) CMD (/usr/bin/true)` — the command is `/usr/bin/true`.

questions.prompt: The module directory holds several rotated log files, including at least one that is compressed. Search all of them — including compressed copies — for an entry containing `FLAG=`. What is the full flag value (everything after `FLAG=`)?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
zgrep 'FLAG=' app.log*
```

`zgrep` transparently decompresses `.gz` files and searches them alongside plain-text logs in a single pass. The flag lives in the oldest compressed rotation `app.log.3.gz`.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes

- Use **`tail -n`** / **`tail -f`** / **`tail -F`** deliberately: bytes vs lines, follow mode, and rotation behavior.
- Use **`less`** as a pager and know **`+F`** (start in forward-follow mode) vs interactive navigation.
- Read **`journalctl`** output shapes and common flags (**`-f`**, **`-b`**, **`-u`**, **`-n`**, **`--no-pager`**) on paper or fixtures before touching a live system.
- Recognize **rotated** filename patterns (**`app.log`**, **`app.log.1`**, **`.gz`**) and where writers append after rotation.

## Scope

**In scope:** local fixtures, conceptual differences Linux vs macOS (no **`journalctl`** on macOS by default). **Out of scope:** shipping production **`logrotate`** configs; full ELK/Loki pipelines.
